title: Finite exceptional adjoints and coefficient change
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_r=A_{E,r}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^r$ for integers $r\ge1$. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism. Work on the small pro-etale sites with the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories $\mathcal C_{T,r}=D^b_{ctf}(T,A_r)$ of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Use the constructible exceptional inverse image $G_r=Rf_r^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the compact-support functor $F_r=Rf_{!,r}$ of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Put $\omega_{T,r}=Ra_T^!A_r$ and $D_{T,r}=R\mathcal Hom_{A_r}(-,\omega_{T,r})$ as in [def-fix-six-functor-datum], and write $f^*=Lf_r^*$ for the ordinary derived pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Then there is a canonical natural isomorphism on $\mathcal C_{Y,r}$
$$Rf_r^!L\cong D_{X,r}f^*D_{Y,r}L.$$
For $m\ge n\ge1$, $L\in\mathcal C_{Y,m}$, and $Q_T=(-)\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$, there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$b_{m,n,L}:Q_X(Rf_m^!L)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_n^!(Q_YL).$$
The maps satisfy the quotient cocycle: after tensor associativity, $b_{m,t}=b_{n,t}\circ(Q_{n,t}b_{m,n})$ for $m\ge n\ge t\ge1$, with the indicated components evaluated at the reduced objects, and $b_{r,r}=\operatorname{id}$. They identify the units $\eta_r:\operatorname{id}\to G_rF_r$ and counits $\epsilon_r:F_rG_r\to\operatorname{id}$ under the canonical compact-support coefficient comparison $q_{m,n}:Q_YF_m\xrightarrow{\sim}F_nQ_X$. Equivalently,
$$G_n(q_{m,n,K})\circ b_{m,n,F_mK}\circ Q_X(\eta_{m,K})=\eta_{n,Q_XK},$$
$$\epsilon_{n,Q_YL}\circ F_n(b_{m,n,L})\circ q_{m,n,G_mL}=Q_Y(\epsilon_{m,L}).$$

proof.text: All adjunctions below are restricted to the stated constructible categories. Choose a compactification $f=pj$ by [thm-nagata-compactification] and use $F_r=Rp_*j_!$ from [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. [lem-trf-open-ctf] puts $j_!K$ in $D^b_{ctf}(\overline X,A_r)$, and [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale], applied to the proper finite-type $p$ and an integer bounding $\dim\overline X$, which exists by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] since $\overline X$ is finite type over $k$, puts $F_rK$ in $\mathcal C_{Y,r}$. Every bounded constructible input is of etale origin by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. Choose its bounded constructible etale witness. If the input has Tor interval $[a,b]$, clause (ii) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] shows that this witness has the same Tor interval on the etale site. Thus every later use of a finite constructible pro-etale realization has a finite-Tor etale witness, not just a bounded constructible one. Hence [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] gives $F_r\dashv G_r$ with its specified compactification comparisons, and clauses (1)--(2) of [thm-sf-preservation-class] give bounded constructibility and $G_r\mathcal C_{Y,r}\subseteq\mathcal C_{X,r}$. More explicitly, take the finite affine chart family in that statement, with $D=0$ for an empty chart family, and $e=\dim Y$ for nonempty $Y$ and $e=0$ otherwise. An input with cohomological interval $[a,b]$ has output interval $[a-2D,b+2e+1]$, and an input with Tor interval $[c,d]$ has output Tor interval $[c-2D,d+2e+1]$. These are assertions about the transported constructible adjoint, not the stronger ambient admissibility datum. The hypotheses are satisfied also for the structure morphisms of $X,Y$, whose targets are $\operatorname{Spec}k$. No unrestricted pro-etale ambient adjoint is required.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: finite exceptional preservation and the already constructed adjoint (agent expansion checked against the main-20261015 Proof)

proof.text: At each finite stage [thm-fix-general-biduality] gives the natural evaluation-defined biduality $\delta_{T,M}:M\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{T,r}D_{T,r}M$ and the contravariant anti-equivalence $D_{T,r}$ on $\mathcal C_{T,r}$, for $T=X,Y$. By [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], $f^*D_{Y,r}L$ is again in $\mathcal C_{X,r}$, so $H_rL=D_{X,r}f^*D_{Y,r}L$ is a well-defined constructible finite-Tor object. Clause (1) of [fix-prop-adjunctions] supplies the ordinary pullback/direct-image adjunction. Only ordinary clause (1) is used. The duals here are also exactly those in the current statement of [cor-coef-finite-verdier]: [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison], applied to each $T=X,Y$ and each positive finite stage $r$, identifies $\nu_T^*(a_T^{\times}A_r)$ with $Ra_T^!A_r$, and identifies the internal-Hom duality, its evaluation pairing and its double-dual map under this identification. Thus both definitions of the pro-etale dual agree canonically. Use the universe-small skeletons in the site definitions, so the smallness hypotheses of the two ringed-site results below hold. We also use the genuine tensor--internal-Hom bijection on these ringed sites. The internal identity $R\mathcal Hom(U,R\mathcal Hom(V,W))\cong R\mathcal Hom(U\otimes^LV,W)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], followed by $H^0$ and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections], gives $\operatorname{Hom}(U,R\mathcal Hom(V,W))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(U\otimes^LV,W)$. It sends a map to its evaluation composite, by the componentwise Hom-complex identity. Tensor products of finite-Tor constructible objects remain in that domain: use [lem-pur-finite-tensor-constructible-cohomology] for constructibility, and bounded flat models from [lem-sf-flat-model]; the total tensor of models in $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$ is flat and supported in $[a+c,b+d]$. These products are therefore valid adjunction inputs.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: duality domains and tensor-Hom transposition (agent expansion checked against the main-20261015 Proof)

proof.text:
Construct the fixed-coefficient exchange without an axiomatized six-functor datum. Write $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $P_{T,r}=Ra_{T!,r}$, and $\operatorname{tr}_{T,r}:P_{T,r}\omega_{T,r}\to A_r$ for the structure-map counit. The inputs are bounded below and have the etale-origin witnesses from step 1, so the current comparison-class version of [thm-sf-comp-composition] applies and gives $\kappa_r:P_{Y,r}F_r\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{X,r}$. Define $\tau_r:F_r\omega_{X,r}\to\omega_{Y,r}$ to be the unique transpose under $P_{Y,r}\dashv Ra_{Y,r}^!$ of $\operatorname{tr}_{X,r}\circ\kappa_{r,\omega_{X,r}}$. Hence
$$\operatorname{tr}_{Y,r}\circ P_{Y,r}(\tau_r)=\operatorname{tr}_{X,r}\circ\kappa_{r,\omega_{X,r}}.$$
Here the adjunction exists by step 1.

For finite-Tor constructible $M$, put $J_r=Rf_{*,r}D_{X,r}M$, finite-Tor constructible by [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale], using an integer bound for $\dim X$ supplied by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Define $E_{r,M}:J_r\to D_{Y,r}F_rM$ to be the tensor-Hom transpose of
$$\lambda_{r,M}:J_r\otimes^LF_rM\xrightarrow{\mathrm{sym}}F_rM\otimes^LJ_r\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}_{f,M,J_r}}F_r(M\otimes^Lf^*J_r)\xrightarrow{F_r(1\otimes\varepsilon^*_{r,D_XM})}F_r(M\otimes^LD_XM)\xrightarrow{F_r(\mathrm{ev}_M\circ\mathrm{sym})}F_r\omega_{X,r}\xrightarrow{\tau_r}\omega_{Y,r}.$$
The projection map is the isomorphism of [fix-prop-projection-formula]; its finite hypotheses are verified in steps 1--2. Evaluation is [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. This explicitly specifies the relative exchange map.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: construct exchange from projection, ordinary counit, evaluation and absolute trace (agent expansion checked against the main-20261015 Proof)

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sf-absolute-trace-exchange] to $\mathcal C_T=\mathcal C_{T,r}$, $\mathcal S=\mathcal C_{s,r}$, $\Omega=A_r$, $P_T=Ra_{T!,r}$, $A_T=Ra_{T,r}^!$, $F=F_r$, $U=f^*$ and $R=Rf_{*,r}$. The absolute adjunctions and their domains are step 1; tensor closure and evaluation-representability are step 2; $\kappa$ and the projection isomorphism $\theta=\mathrm{PF}$ are step 3. Ordinary adjunction is [fix-prop-adjunctions](1). Thus all hypotheses hold on these categories. The lemma's trace transpose and evaluation pairing are exactly $\tau_r,\lambda_{r,M}$ from step 3, so its conclusion proves that the specified $E_{r,M}:Rf_{*,r}D_{X,r}M\to D_{Y,r}F_rM$ is invertible. It also identifies its Hom action, which will fix the normalization used under coefficient change.

Now use the original four Hom bijections with this constructed exchange:
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,H_rL)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^*D_YL,D_XK)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(D_YL,Rf_*D_XK)\\
&\xrightarrow{E_K\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}_Y(D_YL,D_YF_rK)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(F_rK,L).
\end{aligned}$$
The outside arrows are biduality [thm-fix-general-biduality], the middle ordinary adjunction is [fix-prop-adjunctions](1). Explicitly the first sends $u:K\to D_XT$ to $D_X(u)\circ\delta_T$. Denote the inverse composite by $\Phi_r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] this gives $F_r\dashv H_r$. The route remains the imported duality/ordinary-adjunction/exchange route, with the previously conditional exchange proved rather than assumed.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: prove exchange and the four Hom bijections (agent expansion checked against the main-20261015 Proof)

proof.text: Compare the two representing objects explicitly. If $\Psi_r$ is the specified adjunction $F_r\dashv G_r$ from step 1, define $\alpha_{r,L}=\Phi_r(\epsilon_{r,L}):G_rL\to H_rL$ and its reverse $\gamma_{r,L}=\Psi_r(\epsilon^H_{r,L}):H_rL\to G_rL$. Naturality of the Hom bijections gives $\Phi_r(a)=\alpha_{r,L}\circ\Psi_r(a)$ and $\Psi_r(a)=\gamma_{r,L}\circ\Phi_r(a)$. Surjectivity, evaluated on the identity of each representing object, gives $\gamma_r\alpha_r=1$ and $\alpha_r\gamma_r=1$. These same equations show that $\alpha_r$ identifies the units and counits (each is the corresponding identity under the Hom bijection). Thus $\alpha_r:G_r\xrightarrow{\sim}H_r$ is the canonical first isomorphism of the statement.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: uniqueness of the right adjoint, with units and counits (agent expansion checked against the main-20261015 Proof)

proof.text: Write $A=A_m$, $B=A_n$. Reduction $Q_T$ takes $\mathcal C_{T,m}$ to $\mathcal C_{T,n}$. Indeed, [lem-sf-flat-model] supplies a bounded flat representative $P$ for any such input, and [lem-sf-reduction-flat-model] identifies $Q_TK$ with $P\otimes_AB$, flat over $B$ in the same finite interval. Its cohomology is constructible by [lem-pur-finite-tensor-constructible-cohomology], applied to $K$ and the constant finite $A$-module sheaf $B_T$: both are bounded constructible $A$-complexes. Here constructibility as a $B$-module follows from constructibility of the underlying $A$-module: on a stratum with a constant $A$-module description, the stalk is killed by $\ker(A\to B)$, and that description is automatically $B$-linear, since every scalar in $B$ lifts to $A$. Its finite $A$-module stalk is consequently a finite $B$-module stalk. This proves bounded constructibility as well as finite Tor amplitude; it does not assert that the nonflat quotient $A\to B$ is flat.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: domains of the finite coefficient comparisons (agent expansion checked against the main-20261015 Proof)

proof.text:
Let $d_{T,M}:Q_TD_{T,m}M\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{T,n}Q_TM$ be [cor-coef-finite-verdier], with its $(A,B)=(A_m,A_n)$ and its scheme equal to $T=X$ or $Y$. The required hypotheses are the finite-field datum, separated finite-type schemes and positive quotient indices of the statement; the inputs $L$ and $f^*D_{Y,m}L$ are finite-Tor constructible by step 2. Use its pro-etale assertion with the duals identified in step 2. Its quotient cocycle and evaluation/double-dual compatibility are explicitly assertions on this same site.  To fix the evaluation target map explicitly, take $u_T:Q_T\omega_{T,m}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{T,n}$ from [lem-coef-finite-dualizing] and the evaluation-defined $v_{M,\omega_{T,m}}$ of [thm-coef-finite-hom], and use
$$d_{T,M}=R\mathcal Hom_B(Q_TM,u_T)\circ v_{M,\omega_{T,m}}.$$
The second argument is in the finite-Tor constructible category: the constant unit has interval $[0,0]$, and its Verdier dual is $\omega_{T,m}$ by the tensor-Hom unit formula and step 2's duality preservation. Thus the general finite-Hom comparison applies, without site-perfectness. Its evaluation identity and naturality in the target give the explicit equation
$$\mathrm{ev}_{Q_TM}\circ(d_{T,M}\otimes1)=u_T\circ Q_T(\mathrm{ev}_M).$$
This specifies the evaluation-preserving duality comparison used here; its cocycle follows from the cocycles of $v,u$ and naturality in the second variable, as in [cor-coef-finite-verdier]. Transposing this same evaluation identity, with tensor symmetry, gives $d_{T,D_{T,m}M}\circ Q_T\delta_M=D_{T,n}(d_{T,M})\circ\delta_{Q_TM}$: the two transposes are the reduction of $\mathrm{ev}_M$ with its tensor order reversed. In particular the absolute $u_T$ in the relative trace square below is exactly the map in this evaluation identity.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: applying the two coherent duality comparisons and their cocycle (agent expansion checked against the main-20261015 Proof)

proof.text:
Let $p_M:Q_Xf^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*Q_YM$ be the pullback comparison of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Put $V=f^*D_{Y,m}L$ and
$$t_L=f^*(d_{Y,L})\circ p_{D_{Y,m}L}:Q_XV\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*D_{Y,n}Q_YL.$$
The required comparison on the dual formula is
$$h_L=D_{X,n}(t_L^{-1})\circ d_{X,V}:Q_XH_mL\xrightarrow{\sim}H_nQ_YL.$$
The inverse on $t_L$ is essential because $D_X$ is contravariant. Define
$$b_{m,n,L}=\alpha_{n,Q_YL}^{-1}\circ h_L\circ Q_X(\alpha_{m,L}).$$
Each factor is an isomorphism and is natural.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: applying the two coherent duality comparisons and their cocycle (agent expansion checked against the main-20261015 Proof)

proof.text:
For $m\ge n\ge t\ge1$, put $L_m=L$, $L_n=Q_Y^{m,n}L$, $L_t=Q_Y^{n,t}L_n$ and $V_i=f^*D_{Y,i}L_i$; superscripts on $Q,d,t,h$ below specify the coefficient quotient. Insert tensor reassociation throughout. Expanding $t=f^*(d_Y)p$ and using naturality of $p$ gives
$$t^{n,t}_{L_n}\circ Q_X^{n,t}(t^{m,n}_L)=f^*\bigl(d_Y^{n,t}\circ Q_Y^{n,t}(d_Y^{m,n})\bigr)\circ p^{m,t}=t^{m,t}_L,$$
by the $d_Y$ cocycle of [cor-coef-finite-verdier] and the pullback comparison cocycle of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Naturality of $d_X^{n,t}$ for $(t^{m,n}_L)^{-1}:V_n\to Q_X^{m,n}V_m$ then gives
$$\begin{aligned}
h^{n,t}_{L_n}\circ Q_X^{n,t}(h^{m,n}_L)
&=D_{X,t}\bigl(Q_X^{n,t}((t^{m,n}_L)^{-1})\circ(t^{n,t}_{L_n})^{-1}\bigr)\circ d_{X,Q_X^{m,n}V_m}^{n,t}\circ Q_X^{n,t}(d_{X,V_m}^{m,n})\\
&=D_{X,t}((t^{m,t}_L)^{-1})\circ d_{X,V_m}^{m,t}=h^{m,t}_L.
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality uses contravariant functoriality of $D_{X,t}$; the second uses the preceding $t$ identity and the $d_X$ cocycle. Expanding $b=\alpha_n^{-1}hQ_X(\alpha_m)$ twice now cancels the adjacent $Q_X^{n,t}(\alpha_n)$ and $Q_X^{n,t}(\alpha_n^{-1})$, leaving $\alpha_t^{-1}h^{m,t}Q_X^{m,t}(\alpha_m)=b_{m,t}$. This proves the displayed quotient cocycle for $b$. At an identity quotient all comparisons are identities, so $b_{r,r}=1$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: applying the two coherent duality comparisons and their cocycle (agent expansion checked against the main-20261015 Proof)

proof.text:
Use the compact-support comparison $q_K:Q_YF_mK\xrightarrow{\sim}F_nQ_XK$ of [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. For ordinary direct image use $c_M:Q_YRf_{*,m}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,n}Q_XM$ of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], with its coefficient ring $A=A_m$ and its finite commutative $A$-algebra $B=A_n$, applied to finite-Tor constructible $M=D_{X,m}K$. The quotient $A_m\to A_n$ is finite as an $A_m$-module because $A_n$ is cyclic; no flatness of this quotient is needed. Use the theorem's finite constructible pro-etale realization on the finite-Tor etale-origin witnesses of step 1. Its stated definition of $c$ as the scalar extension of the ordinary counit supplies exactly the following identity. Let $p_M:Q_Xf_m^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}f_n^*Q_YM$. The ordinary-counit identity is
$$\varepsilon^*_{n,Q_XM}\circ f_n^*(c_M)\circ p_{Rf_{*,m}M}=Q_X(\varepsilon^*_{m,M}),$$
with pullback/tensor source identifications inserted. This is exactly the transpose defining the canonical projection map $c$ in [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]. Thus the ordinary Hom bijection respects finite reduction; no finite ordinary-direct-image assertion is taken from [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. The same operation-reduction statement and [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] preserve the projection construction and tensor constraints used in $\lambda$; [fix-prop-projection-formula] identifies that construction with the finite projection isomorphism. The ordinary counit identity is supplied by [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]; [lem-fix-operation-reduction] is used here only for the pullback, tensor constraints, and projection-construction comparisons on finite-Tor inputs. Its clause requiring admissible exceptional adjoints is not used.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: ordinary adjunction and projection under coefficient change (agent expansion checked against the main-20261015 Proof)

proof.text:
Prove the relative trace square. Let $u_T:Q_T\omega_{T,m}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{T,n}$ be [lem-coef-finite-dualizing] on the pro-etale realization, using the identification of step 2. Its explicitly stated absolute counit equation is
$$\operatorname{tr}_{T,n}\circ P_{T,n}(u_T)\circ q_{a_T,\omega_{T,m}}=Q_s(\operatorname{tr}_{T,m}).$$
We claim
$$\tau_n\circ F_n(u_X)\circ q_{f,\omega_{X,m}}=u_Y\circ Q_Y(\tau_m).\tag{*}$$
Both sides go from $Q_YF_m\omega_{X,m}$ to $\omega_{Y,n}$. Transpose them under $P_{Y,n}\dashv Ra_{Y,n}^!$. Precompose both resulting maps with the isomorphism $q_{a_Y,F_m\omega_{X,m}}:Q_sP_{Y,m}F_m\omega_{X,m}\to P_{Y,n}Q_YF_m\omega_{X,m}$. The left side, using step 3's defining equation for $\tau_n$ and naturality of composition, becomes
$$\operatorname{tr}_{X,n}\circ P_{X,n}(u_X)\circ\kappa_n\circ P_{Y,n}(q_{f,\omega_{X,m}})\circ q_{a_Y,F_m\omega_{X,m}}.$$
By [lem-sf-compact-coefficient-composition] at $(g,f)=(a_Y,f)$ the last three factors equal $q_{a_X,\omega_{X,m}}\circ Q_s(\kappa_m)$. The absolute counit identity for $X$ therefore makes the expression $Q_s(\operatorname{tr}_{X,m}\circ\kappa_m)$. The right transpose, by naturality of $q_{a_Y}$ and the absolute counit identity for $Y$, is
$$Q_s(\operatorname{tr}_{Y,m}\circ P_{Y,m}(\tau_m))=Q_s(\operatorname{tr}_{X,m}\circ\kappa_m).$$
Cancel the precomposition isomorphism and use injectivity of the adjunction bijection to get (*). This proves the required relative trace compatibility from absolute dualizing comparisons; it never assumes a coefficient comparison for $Rf^!$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: independent relative trace square (agent expansion checked against the main-20261015 Proof)

proof.text:
Prove the independent relative exchange square by transposing its two sides, using step 3's explicit pairing. For $M\in\mathcal C_{X,m}$ put $J_m=Rf_{*,m}D_{X,m}M$ and
$$j_M=Rf_{*,n}(d_{X,M})\circ c_{D_{X,m}M}:Q_YJ_m\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,n}D_{X,n}Q_XM.$$
The asserted equality is
$$d_{Y,F_mM}\circ Q_Y(E_{m,M})=D_{Y,n}(q_M)\circ E_{n,Q_XM}\circ j_M.\tag{**}$$
Both sides have source $Q_YJ_m$ and target $D_{Y,n}(Q_YF_mM)$. Tensor-Hom transposition is injective (step 2). By the explicit evaluation identity of step 7 and [cor-coef-finite-verdier], the left transpose is $u_Y\circ Q_Y(\lambda_{m,M})$. The right transpose is
$$\lambda_{n,Q_XM}\circ(j_M\otimes q_M):Q_YJ_m\otimes_B^LQ_YF_mM\to\omega_{Y,n}.$$
Expand this last expression in the order of step 3. Naturality of symmetry and the projection transformation, with its coefficient identity from step 10, move $j_M$ and $q_M$ past the first two factors. The ordinary-counit identity of step 10 replaces $f_n^*c$ followed by the new counit by the reduction of the old counit; naturality of the counit moves $d_{X,M}$ to the evaluation argument. Evaluation compatibility of [cor-coef-finite-verdier] then replaces evaluation after $d_{X,M}$ by $u_X\circ Q_X(\mathrm{ev}_M)$. Thus the whole transpose is
$$\tau_n\circ F_n(u_X)\circ q_{f,\omega_{X,m}}\circ Q_Y\bigl(F_m(\mathrm{ev}_M\circ\mathrm{sym})\circ F_m(1\otimes\varepsilon^*_{m,D_XM})\circ\mathrm{PF}_m\circ\mathrm{sym}\bigr).$$
Equation (*) of step 11 turns this into $u_Y\circ Q_Y(\lambda_{m,M})$, exactly the left transpose. This proves (**). Every factor has now been compared using ordinary adjunctions, projection, evaluation, and absolute traces. Neither thm-sf-verdier-exchange nor any clause of def-sf-datum, including A5, is a premise of this proof.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: independent reduction square for relative Verdier exchange (agent expansion checked against the main-20261015 Proof)

proof.text:
The four Hom bijections in step 4 respect reduction of actual morphisms. For the anti-equivalence arrows, use the explicit formula $u\mapsto D(u)\circ\delta$ and the double-dual equality supplied by [cor-coef-finite-verdier]:
$$d_{T,D_{T,m}N}\circ Q_T(\delta_{T,m,N})=D_{T,n}(d_{T,N})\circ\delta_{T,n,Q_TN}.$$
Both maps have source $Q_TN$ and target $D_{T,n}(Q_TD_{T,m}N)$; naturality of $d$ and this equality compare the arrows. The ordinary-adjunction arrow is step 10, and the exchange arrow is the independently proved (**) of step 12. Consequently, for every $a:F_mK\to L$,
$$h_L\circ Q_X(\Phi_m(a))=\Phi_n(Q_Y(a)\circ q_K^{-1}).$$
This compares reduction of a given morphism, not a tensor of Hom groups. In step 5's comparison notation, take $K=G_mL$ and $a=\epsilon_{m,L}$, so $\Phi_m(a)=\alpha_{m,L}$. By step 8's definition of $b$, cancelling $\alpha_{n,Q_YL}$ shows
$$b_L=G_n(Q_Y\epsilon_{m,L})\circ G_n(q_{G_mL}^{-1})\circ\eta_{n,Q_XG_mL}.$$
The right side is precisely the mate of $q^{-1}:F_nQ_X\to Q_YF_m$ under the given exceptional adjunctions, by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Thus the isomorphism constructed with the two duals is the specified exceptional coefficient comparison.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: comparison of Hom bijections and identification of the mate (agent expansion checked against the main-20261015 Proof)

proof.text:
Finally apply the defining transpose and inverse-transpose formulas of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] to the equality just proved. The transpose of $b$ is $Q_Y\epsilon_m\circ q_{G_m}^{-1}$, which gives
$$\epsilon_{n,Q_YL}\circ F_n(b_L)\circ q_{G_mL}=Q_Y\epsilon_{m,L}.$$
For the unit identity, substitute the mate formula from step 13 and use naturality of $\eta_n$ at $Q_X(\eta_{m,K})$. Then naturality of $q^{-1}$ at $\eta_{m,K}:K\to G_mF_mK$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
b_{F_mK}\circ Q_X\eta_{m,K}
&=G_n\bigl(Q_Y\epsilon_{m,F_mK}\circ q_{G_mF_mK}^{-1}\circ F_n(Q_X\eta_{m,K})\bigr)\circ\eta_{n,Q_XK}\\
&=G_n\bigl(Q_Y(\epsilon_{m,F_mK}\circ F_m\eta_{m,K})\circ q_K^{-1}\bigr)\circ\eta_{n,Q_XK}\\
&=G_n(q_K^{-1})\circ\eta_{n,Q_XK}.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is the triangle identity $\epsilon_{m,F_mK}\circ F_m(\eta_{m,K})=1$. Composing with $G_n(q_K)$ now gives
$$G_n(q_K)\circ b_{F_mK}\circ Q_X\eta_{m,K}=\eta_{n,Q_XK}.$$
These are precisely both identities in the statement. They hold before any inverse-limit reconstruction. Together with steps 7--9 they prove all clauses.
